newsitem.title: NIGERIA: No bodies found a week after Nigerian plane crash.
newsitem.headline: No bodies found a week after Nigerian plane crash.

text.p: Rescuers have recovered limbs but no full bodies from a Nigerian plane that crashed into the lagoon a week ago killing all 142 people on board, officials said, on Thursday.

Peter Igbinedion, chief executive of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), told reporters that the three engines, the tail and some smaller parts of the Boeing 727 had been recovered from the crash site east of Lagos, the state news agency reported.
"This systematic search of the area will continue until the whole of the aircraft wreckage has been recovered," he said.
A FAAN official said: "So far no bodies have been found, limbs and other bits have been recovered but no full body has been found."
The area of the crash is dense mangrove swamp called Ejirin, some 40 kms (25 miles) northeast of Lagos.
Relatives of the plane operated by Aviation Development Company have been angry that it has taken Nigerian rescue authorities so long to search for the remains of the victims.
One has threatened to sue if the body of his brother was not found and produced for burial.
But Igbinedion said: "We sincerely believe that the best effort has been made in the fastest possible time to recover the aircraft wreckage."

The ADC flight, coming from the southeastern oil city of Port Harcourt, lost contact minutes before it was due to land in Lagos last Thursday evening. Among the casualties were about 30 foreigners of different nationalities.
